P1.evidence: Setter notes used repeatedly and specifically: 'I've heard a lot of great things already from Derek', then 'Derek already mentioned something about that' on nutrition, then 'you also mentioned something with sweets, et cetera. Does that ring a bell?' No four-part frame — the opening was a fit frame only: 'If it's a good fit, let's get started. If it's not the best fit, also perfectly fine.' Agreement obtained. Open question asked verbatim.

P2.evidence: Injuries and training were done properly. 'Any sort of inflexibilities that you have at the moment, mobility issues, something that comes up for you or not really?' followed by a one-to-ten scale and a pattern probe surfaced the lower back and hamstrings. Nutrition was probed to frequency (Mexican bread two to three days a week, processed versus ultra-processed). But age was never asked at all, height and weight were never asked, health conditions were never asked, sleep and energy were never asked, and occupation surfaced only because the prospect volunteered 'I sell AC'.

P3.evidence: The bridge was asked properly: 'what I see a lot with people is that there's always like a mental side on it as well... so do you have like a bigger why for yourself?' The future-state question ran too. But Phase 3 never got past the individual — the deepest answer obtained was 'share my story with people, you know, my friends and tell them, hey, this happened, it's pretty cool, follow this guy.' A girlfriend and an international move were both on the table and neither was ever connected to the goal.

P4.evidence: The best Phase 4 work so far in the batch. 'What have you tried in those two years?' and then the root-cause question asked directly: 'why did you not follow through with the calisthenics if I may ask?' followed by 'Why not?' on the gym aversion. The prospect then handed over the gap himself — 'the ball will be in my court of following through' — and the rep answered with reassurance rather than excavation: 'are you not actually planning on following through with it as well?' That is the inverse of P4f.

P5.evidence: No two-year question, no why-not, no line in the sand. Willingness to settle was asserted rather than asked: 'it sounds like you're not really willing to settle for a life where it doesn't work better.' No cost of inaction was established anywhere, which is why $6,000 met a $400 expectation with nothing in between.

P6.evidence: P6a ran cleanly: 'What's like the thing that you feel like, yeah, this gives me the confidence that I'll be able to get there with this coaching?' P6b was a product-fit check rather than an all-in check — 'do you feel like, yeah, this is what I'm looking for?' — and never touched capacity. He got a yes about the product and presented into a hard financial no.

P11.evidence: Payment was collected on the call, though for the $200 community rather than the programme: 'So I see that you just paid.' No Trevor onboarding applies to the community product. No agreement was sent or signed. Onboarding was handled well for the product actually sold — the Skool link was sent in the Zoom chat, the account was created live and the community, classroom and calendar tabs were walked through — but there was no welcome email or onboarding questionnaire.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran: 'Outside of the investment piece, do you feel like, yeah, I do want to get started with this, but it's just a big amount?' The worth-it test ran. Budget expectation was extracted ($300-400 for six months). Credit card and credit score were asked (650). Never ran: cash on hand, monthly leftover after bills, how many credit cards, available credit per card, used versus available, crypto/stocks/investments. The 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' reframe never appeared, and the rep hinted the price itself was flexible with 'No, it could also be less, right?'

Trigger present: the November move to Mexico and 'that's gonna cost me a lot of money to move out there'. No scripted move ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep accepted the timing constraint and moved on.

Two script gaps. First, the self-sufficiency objection — 'if there wasn't a way to get there by myself, and there is' — which has no play and which the rep conceded outright. Second, an anchor at roughly $80 a year from a prior online programme, fifteen times below the six-month price, with no scripted path for repositioning a category price expectation.

notes: Phase 4 was the strongest yet and Phase 5 was absent, and the gap between the two decided the call: the rep found the root cause and then never made not fixing it cost anything. The clearest single correction is that the prospect said 'that's how much my bike costs' about $6,000 — evidence he has made a $6,000 discretionary purchase before — and the rep let it pass as an objection rather than using it. Second correction: the close, the downsell and the onboarding for a $200 subscription were executed better than the $6,000 offer was ever defended.
